name: Uzeda
label: Touch and Go
lede: In 1991 a noise band from Catania mailed a demo to Steve Albini, and he got on a plane to Sicily. Nearly four decades on, three of the five founders are still in the band, and still doing it on their own terms.

hero.by: Uzeda at All Tomorrow's Parties, 2004. Photo: neonwar, Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: Named after a city gate
eras.text: Uzeda took its name from Porta Uzeda, the Baroque gate off Catania's cathedral square, and spent its first years playing a jagged, dynamic rock that nobody in Sicily was asking for. The move that changed everything was a cassette in an envelope addressed to Chicago.

years.src: Wikipedia: Uzeda · John Peel Wiki · Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda
years.h: Five musicians in Catania start a band and call it Uzeda
years.p: [[Giovanna Cacciola|4b68e65a-a6a8-460d-bf25-3f8f0add7410]] sings, [[Agostino Tilotta|ade69871-3003-448f-b899-88baf87076f5]] and [[Giovanni Nicosia|ca41a1b7-6afa-4619-a49b-a4dcd020f59e]] play guitar, [[Raffaele Gulisano|b4955f0e-4641-407d-a1f4-53da0501bd7e]] plays bass and [[Davide Oliveri|e83a7f52-30c1-4791-93a3-de74bba5b71d]] drums. The name comes from Porta Uzeda, an 18th-century gate in the city.
years.xp: Cacciola and Tilotta are married, according to the John Peel Wiki. Tilotta, Cacciola and Oliveri are still in the band nearly four decades on.

years.src: AllMusic: Uzeda · Wikipedia: Uzeda
years.h: Out of Colours comes out on Rome's A.V. Arts
years.p: The debut, on a small Rome label the band stayed with for two albums. AllMusic's Mark Deming hears jagged guitars, rifle-shot drums and a ferocious use of dynamics.

years.src: Rockol · IMDb: Uzeda - Do It Yourself · Maria Arena: Uzeda - Do it yourself · Rolling Stone Italia
years.h: From Sicily, a demo tape goes to Steve Albini
years.p: Uzeda mails a cassette to [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] in Chicago. He doesn't send a polite note back: he decides to fly to Catania and record them.
years.xp:
Maria Arena's documentary is built around this moment: a band with no industry connections taking a shot in the dark, and the start of a working friendship that ran until Albini's death in 2024. Within months of the session, the IMDb synopsis notes, the band had a deal with Touch and Go and two BBC sessions.

Tilotta told Rolling Stone Italia how he found Albini before the internet: Touch and Go records printed a phone number, so he called it from a Catania phone booth, feeding it tokens. Scott Giampino picked up at the label: "Don't worry, I'll give you his number."

eras.title: The only Italians on Peel's bill since PFM
eras.text: Albini's first Uzeda record turned a local band into an international one. Within two years they had two John Peel sessions, a record on Touch and Go, and a guitarist fewer.

years.src: Rockol · Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda · AllMusic: Uzeda · Segnali Sonori (2024) · Il Cibicida
years.h: Albini records Waters in Catania
years.p: The second album, still on A.V. Arts, and the turn toward noise rock. Albini recorded every Uzeda album from here on, except the Peel sessions.
years.xp: Albini turned up in Catania with a suitcase to record it, Segnali Sonori recalled, the start of three decades of sessions. He worked as engineer, not producer, Tilotta stressed to Il Cibicida in 2008.

years.src: John Peel Wiki
years.h: Peel calls Uzeda his first Italian session band. He's wrong
years.p: On air, [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] says Uzeda will be the first Italian band to record a session for him, forgetting PFM had done one in 1973. He blames Ken Garner's book on the sessions.

years.src: John Peel Wiki · Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda
years.h: Uzeda records its first Peel session in London
years.p: Six songs, broadcast on June 11. A second session follows on November 6, aired December 16, which makes Uzeda the only Italian band besides PFM with two.
years.xp: Uzeda was also the only Italian act to have its Peel sessions released commercially: Strange Fruit, the BBC session label, put them out as The Peel Sessions.

years.src: Wikipedia: Uzeda · AllMusic: Uzeda
years.h: Strange Fruit issues The Peel Sessions
years.p: The only Uzeda record of the era Albini didn't engineer, cut by BBC staff in London.

years.src: Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda · AllMusic: Uzeda · Il Cibicida
years.h: Down to one guitar, Uzeda debuts on Touch and Go with 4
years.p: Nicosia has left. The EP is the band's first release on Corey Rusk's Chicago label, which would carry them for the next decade.
years.xp: Tilotta told Il Cibicida in 2008 that Uzeda were the first European band on Touch and Go's full roster, and counted more than 1,300 concerts since 1987.

eras.title: A break that isn't a breakup
eras.text: After Different Section Wires the band stopped making records for eight years without ever calling it quits. The members went off in pairs: Tilotta and Cacciola to a new band with a Pittsburgh drummer, Oliveri and Gulisano into film scores and pop records.

years.src: AllMusic: Uzeda · Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda
years.h: Different Section Wires, recorded with Albini in France
years.p: The first full Uzeda album on Touch and Go. After the tour for it the band takes an eight-year break from recording.

years.src: Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda · Rolling Stone Italia
years.h: Cacciola and Tilotta start Bellini with Don Caballero's Damon Che
years.p: Bellini releases Snowing Sun in 2002 and Small Stones in 2005, with [[Damon Che|8e999c8c-ea9d-4181-8611-60f03a67360b]] of [[Don Caballero|b93697af-a318-417a-b16e-a9eb47fbe2f8]] on drums.
years.xp:
The rhythm section kept busy too: Oliveri and Gulisano played on Gianna Nannini's Aria (2002) and Pia come la canto io (2007) and composed music for Enzo D'Alò's animated film Momo alla conquista del tempo.

Nannini had read about Uzeda in a magazine on a plane, Rolling Stone Italia reported, and got in touch hoping for an introduction to Albini.

years.src: Wikimedia Commons: Uzeda at ATP 2004
years.h: Mid-break, Uzeda turns up at All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: No new record, but still a live band: photos on Wikimedia Commons show them on the ATP stage in 2004.

eras.title: Thirteen years between albums, and nobody in a hurry
eras.text: Stella ended the silence in 2006, then the band went quiet on record again until 2019. In between they threw themselves a 30th birthday in Catania, and Shellac, the Ex and the Black Heart Procession came to play it.

years.cap: Uzeda at Touch and Go's 25th anniversary, the Hideout, Chicago, September 9, 2006
years.src: Touch and Go: Uzeda · Wikipedia: Uzeda
years.h: Stella, cut by Albini at Red House in Senigallia
years.p: The return album, recorded on the Adriatic coast at Red House Recording Studio. Touch and Go's page calls the band's music intense and uncompromising, shaped by their volcanic home.

years.cap: Uzeda at the Covo Club, Bologna, November 3, 2007
years.src: Wikipedia (Italian): Uzeda
years.h: Cacciola sings with Japan's Mono on The Phoenix Tree
years.p: A guest spot for Uzeda's singer on an EP by the Tokyo instrumental band [[Mono|ffe02aed-ef7e-4736-a186-c2f1dd55ce8d]].

years.cap: Uzeda at their 30th anniversary nights, Catania, May 25, 2018
years.src: Rockol · AllMusic: Uzeda · John Peel Wiki · Rolling Stone Italia
years.h: For their 30th, Uzeda bring Shellac and the Ex to Catania
years.p: Two nights at Afrobar with [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]], [[The Ex|ea19687e-8d08-4abe-901e-3135269e4f74]], [[The Black Heart Procession|fd0f1d5f-5d8c-4fcd-9d3c-0c9f20cddc08]], [[June of 44|56f3de75-2c88-4054-a1df-65c661f4ee0f]] and Three Second Kiss. AllMusic says the party gave the band new energy.
years.xp:
The anniversary shows are in Maria Arena's documentary, which she shot between 2016 and 2020. Uzeda's members have long refused to treat the band as a job; music can't be reduced to "a salary," as they put it.

About 1,500 people came each night, the band told Rolling Stone Italia.

years.src: XtraCult · Temporary Residence: Quocumque jeceris stabit
years.h: Three days in Verona for a new album
years.p: Uzeda tracks its first album in 13 years in Verona in three days, with Albini engineering, and the documentary crew filming.

years.src: Temporary Residence: Quocumque jeceris stabit · God Is in the TV
yt: Live at Circolo della Musica, Turin, 2019
years.h: Quocumque jeceris stabit, on Temporary Residence
years.p: Latin for roughly "wherever you throw it, it will stand." Thirty-one minutes, recorded "as always" by Albini, the label says.

eras.title: Without Albini, with a film
eras.text: Albini's death in May 2024 came weeks before the film about the band he championed premiered. A year later Uzeda changed bassists for the first time in 38 years and kept touring.

years.src: Wikipedia: Steve Albini · Rockol · Segnali Sonori (2024)
years.h: Steve Albini dies at 61
years.p: The engineer who answered Uzeda's demo, recorded nearly every record they made, and played their 30th birthday with Shellac, dies of a heart attack in Chicago.
years.xp: "Knowing Steve Albini was a great fortune in life," Tilotta told Segnali Sonori the day after. He called the loss "infinite."

years.src: Maria Arena: Uzeda - Do it yourself · Rockol · XtraCult · Università di Catania · Rolling Stone Italia
yt: Uzeda: Do It Yourself, teaser with English subtitles
years.h: Maria Arena's Uzeda: Do It Yourself premieres in Bologna
years.p: A 102-minute portrait of the band, crowdfunded in 2023, opens at Biografilm Festival, then reaches Italian cinemas that autumn and the Catania Film Fest on October 3.
years.xp:
The film follows the band from the 1991 demo through Peel, Touch and Go and three decades of touring in their own van with their own gear, the way the University of Catania's archive describes their European tours. It went to streaming on OpenDDB on July 7, 2025, and played the Chicago Underground Film Festival.

The crowdfunding raised 20,000 euros, and the film took eight years from first shoot to screen, Rolling Stone Italia reported.

years.src: Segnali Sonori
years.h: Gulisano out, jazz bassist Vincenzo Virgillito in
years.p: Uzeda's first bass change since 1987. Virgillito had subbed for Gulisano at a Messina show in 2022; he calls learning the parts the hardest test he's taken as a musician.
years.xp: He says the band called him directly: "We need you, we've settled things with Raffaele." His first shows were in Florence, Savona, Bari and Naples in late May and June 2025, and he describes Uzeda's songs as rigid, like classical scores.

years.src: Segnali Sonori
yt: Uzeda live at BLO Kantine, Berlin, April 25, 2026
years.h: Uzeda plays Berlin's BLO Kantine, still on its own terms
years.p: The new line-up plays Berlin in April and Piacenza's Desert Fox Fest on May 30. In 2025 Virgillito said new songs and an album were in the works.
